last_completed_unit.target: Cargo vendor command behavior and vendor-directory materialization contract
last_completed_unit.result: Official pinned Cargo documentation verifies that cargo vendor vendors crates.io and git dependencies into a selected local directory, prints the configuration needed to consume those vendored sources, --locked requires the existing Cargo.lock dependency resolution to remain exact, --offline forbids network access and relies on locally available material, and --frozen combines locked plus offline semantics. The command therefore defines a quota-independent local vendoring mechanism in principle, but this invocation did not establish a scheduled-Chat-native Cargo process executor or actually materialize a vendor directory.

source_scope: Frozen required controls at note main 3055c5dac54a9e9b122a3d5d4385297c5efd8579; own open_source LATEST worker_revision 350; exactly one official pinned rust-lang/cargo source body at commit 7941be6fb416b4cd9666aef7b858dfea25587a8c. No second public source and no Cargo execution. No O, downstream, other-worker, legacy, shared-ledger, or other-role semantic content was consumed.
scope_guard: Evidence is limited to the pinned cargo vendor documentation. It does not prove cargo vendor can execute inside scheduled Chat, that required dependency/index material is already local for any concrete project, that a vendor directory was actually materialized, that a vendored build/test can run offline here, or that richer-mode outcome parity is achieved.
